pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Sugar and Spice
work.note: Sugar and Spice é uma rima infantil inglesa de tradição oral, registrada em coletâneas a partir do início do século XIX. Os versos dizem de que são feitas as meninas, enquanto outra estrofe tradicional diz de que são feitos os meninos. Não há autor conhecido, e o texto circula em variações. pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: An ice cream shop in Savannah gives you many small choices: flavor, number of scoops, and cup or cone. Learn to choose fast and enjoy it slowly.

facts.big: You can choose two different flavors in one order.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: Two scoops can be two flavors, like chocolate and strawberry.

facts.big: A “scoop” is one round ball of ice cream.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: The shop uses a scoop tool to make each ball.

facts.big: Savannah is in the state of Georgia.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: It is a historic port city, founded in 1733.

facts.big: “Sugar and Spice” is a very old rhyme that is still repeated today.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: It comes from oral tradition and was printed in the early 1800s.

compare.br: In Brazil, you often choose a sorvete by weight in a self-serve shop, or an açaí bowl with toppings.
compare.us: In the USA, many shops sell by the scoop, in a cup or a cone, and the server puts it together for you.
compare.tip: Say the flavor first, then the number of scoops.
compare.ask: What is your favorite flavor? Say it in English.

pages.title: A sweet afternoon · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot day in **Savannah**. My friend Tess and I walk past an old square. We see a small ice cream shop. I have a **sweet tooth**, so I say, “**Let’s go in!**”

The server, Tiana, smiles. “**Hi! What flavor do you want?**” I say, “**Chocolate, please.**” “**One scoop or two?**” “**Two scoops. And strawberry.**” She asks, “**In a cup or a cone?**” “**A cone, please.**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: A sweet afternoon · 2/3
paragraphs: Tiana makes the ice cream with a round tool. First chocolate, then strawberry. It looks great! “**That’s four dollars**,” she says. “**Here you go. Thanks!**” I say. “**Enjoy your ice cream!**” she says.
Tess chooses vanilla in a cup. We sit on a bench and eat. The sun is hot, so the ice cream melts fast! We laugh and clean our hands with a napkin. “This is **so good**!” says Tess.

pages.title: A sweet afternoon · 3/3
paragraphs: I remember the old rhyme Sugar and Spice. It is a nice idea for a sweet day: sugar, cream and friends. A scoop of vanilla, a cherry on top. “**Why not?**” Tess says. “**Let’s get another.**”

pages.title: Palavras pelo contexto

items.q: The ice cream melts fast in the sun. O que significa “melts”?
items.why: Melt = change from solid to liquid.

items.q: She has a sweet tooth. O que significa “sweet tooth”?
items.why: A sweet tooth = loves sweet foods.

items.q: We sit on a bench in the shade. O que significa “bench”?
items.why: A bench is a long seat for people.
